The compressor had a design speed of 21,789 ft/s (exit tip speed of 1615 ft/s)
The impeller had 15 blade/splitter pairs with spanwise varying backsweep, lean, and elliptical leading and trailing edges
The diffuser had 20 vane/splitter pairs with the splitters offset to maximize pressure recovery
The exit guide vanes (EGVs) had 60 cascade-style airfoils
The measured stage pressure ratio at the design point was 4.68 ± 0.0074, compared to the design intent of 4.80
The measured adiabatic efficiency at the design point was 82.2% ± 1.1%, compared to the design intent of 88.8%
The measured stability margin was 7.5%, compared to the 12% design intent
The measured work factor was 0.81, compared to the design intent of 0.7905
The impeller exit corrected flow rate was lower than the design intent at the same operating condition
The diffuser static pressure rise was lower than the design intent, with a minimum loss point at a lower flow rate
The diffuser vane loading diagrams showed the splitter vanes were operating at a large negative incidence
The probe data in the vaneless space did not adequately resolve the pressure flow field compared to the vane leading edge measurements
The comprehensive data sets and geometry from this study will be made publicly available
The root-cause analysis of the performance shortfall will continue to guide future design efforts
The test facility (CE-18) could provide up to 6000 hp, 60,000 rpm, 30:1 pressure ratio, and 20-inch diameter test articles
